reviews.text: If you like me grew up on Wizardry, Might and Magic, or Eye of the Beholder and have been chasing that feeling ever since, stop searching. This is it. Titans of the Past doesn't just understand what made those classics great. It builds on them thoughtfully. What I love the most is "The Customization". Game really shines herre. Building your party goes way beyond picking four classes. Unlockable races, classes, spells, gear, name it. You keep finding new synergies dozens of hours in. My current run uses a party composition I never would have considered when I started, it's emerging. Albeit, you can go all in on heavy pre-planning of the run, I just never bother and Titans still play great! Town development and crafting add another layer without feeling tacked on. Dungeon delving feeds into your town, your town feeds back into better dungeon runs. Simple loop, but it works. There's also actual lore here worth uncovering. The name has a double meaning, and piecing it together has been surprisingly rewarding. Not gonna spoil stuff! This is a love letter to old school dungeon crawlers, made by people who clearly played them obsessively. Highly recommended.

I've been following this game from the first demo. Snuck around on reddit, and been waiting on this game since that first peek at it. Bought the game this morning, loaded up a stream, and spent the next 15 hours playing it, testing things out and chatting with the devs over most of that time. I must say the devs were super helpful, and were well informed about their game. They are on the ball, and the small launch issues that popped up here and there they are already busy working on, and in 15 hours of gameplay, I did not face any game breaking, or game crashing bugs at all, I never rebooted the game in the entire 15 hours, and played actively the entire time. I was extremely positively surprised with how stable and smooth the experience was. For the gameplay, it has a massive amount of classes, skills, spells, and abilities. Lots of races, tons of viable builds. The content takes a long time to digest, and there is plenty of unlocks underway letting you change your approach to how you build your characters. There are plenty of deep mechanics, stat impacts, and balancing choices that you can fine tune to make the build your own. Not all of it is fully obvious, but of the ones spotted, it sounds like they are hard at work already to make it even more accessible to play. The stat depth plays in many ways like an rpg of old. You can play cookie cutter builds, and do well. Or you can deep dive and adjust things to make something that works just like you want it. There are a good selection of enemies, special attacks, special buffs, map mutators, and secrets. Just like in the old school games, you need to identify the important enemies in a fight, control or kill them depending on what they are doing. There is a surprising amount of depth here, and at 15 hours I am just scratching the surface on many parts of it. And it sounds like it will only get better going forward, as the devs are active when it comes to getting on bug fixes and gameplay adjustments. If you like tinkering with classes, picking enemies apart systematically, a mixture of real time and time stop mechanics, and putting together fun builds, I definitely recommend buying the game. And even with a limited QA group before release, they have done a great job, with a surprising level of stability and lack of errors many much larger game studios fail to deliver.

This is a frustrating one. I love this game. This game has a lot of potential and I really enjoyed it, but the roadmap is leading me to believe they're winding down a bit too much after release. This feels like REALLY early access, and the roadmap looks like the developers think they're done. The gameplay is fun. I love the style of combat mixed with RPG elements and the time-stopping strategy feel to it. Gear crafting is OP and scratches the power fantasy itch. Pros: - Some cool class variety. - Combat style is great. - Full Diablo style loot+equipment system. - Character building is fun. I always love some good theorycrafting. Cons: - There are no boss monsters. Just the occasional elites. - Enemy variety is paltry. The loading screen has a gelatinous cube and it doesn't even exist. 2 adventures and I guarantee you've seen all the enemies in the game. - Very few maps. Roadmap only shows addition of 2 more. - "Quests" are just complete each difficulty dungeon on every character, numbered 1-40. - Stat "bonuses" are DND style with milestones, meaning later in the game you could add 9 strength and get zero benefit until that 10th strength is added, and the bonus cap ends at 150 stats. It doesn't particularly mix well with Diablo style gear/skills adding percentage to stats. There are so many ways to get overpowered from crafting that these limitations seem arbitrary and limit choice. - No inventory sort, but at least there's a filter. - Physical spells are limited to your class. The only skills you can learn from the thieves guild and the stronghold are your class skills. So pure physical combat characters only have up to 3 different spells, which feels bad. - Spell balance between the schools is way off. Late game, even as a grandmaster, some skills just scale so horribly that they become unusable. Devs need to exclusively play each spell school to see how they feel. There's no way they've done this. - Massively overpowered skills dwarf all the other skills, especially late game. The worst, Grandmaster Bard, has an insta-kill song (aura) that plays for 2 minutes, ignores immunities, and has no limit to what it can kill. This skill needs to be completely overhauled. - Random collectibles around the map don't scale with difficulty, and the paltry resources (usually 1-2) you do get pale in comparison to even tier 1 adventure shrine purchases where you can buy anywhere from 1-30 (and 4 purchase options per shrine), and you almost always have enough currency to buy all of them. Collectibles don't feel good. - There's inconsistency with how skills work. Most skills increase stats additively, some skills lose their tier 1 and 2 bonuses when you upgrade to tier 3 (spell mastery), some skills have typos in what their bonuses actually apply (resistance) - The fountain EXP transfer function (late game function) has an extreme resource cost that makes it borderline unusable. It costs 250 of every resource to bring a level 1 to level 10. It costs like 3 resources to increase your gears' enchantment tier. - The "arena" maps having these random spawn points is stupid. Enemies just teleport in the middle of the map preventing you from taking a defensive position anywhere. - Rats are so GD annoying in this game. Rats that sit back in brush casting fireballs and meteors shouldn't be a thing. Make rats behave like rats. Have humanoid monsters exclusively cast spells. Bats casting blood magic is annoying too, but at least it semi makes sense and can be likened to vampirism. Bats being as tanky as humanoids shouldn't be a thing either though. Features I want: - Add a lock for items you don't want sold. - Add boss rooms. Make bosses immune to instant kill/enslave, and progressively resistant to hard disables. - Revamp fire spells. Too many enemies have natural ~95% fire resistance, and too many fire spells can kill your own team. No other element has these problems. Meteor shower is a tiny radius with way too long of an activation period. Also, fix the "Jumping Fire" spell tooltip, wtf. Grandmaster "Incinerate" is absolutely horrible in every way. - Ground target radius spells should show the size of the area being affected. - Remove the Grandmaster Bard skill, for the love of god. - Turn shift into an active blocking mechanic. Blocks made in this way force the damage onto the active character and yield a brief recovery time. Maybe scale the recovery time with a new Block skill. - Percentage damage reduction added to blocks instead of simply increasing physical resistance for that damage instance. Current block implementation feels bad. - Physical schools of magic for Stronghold and Thieves Guild. - Add unarmed weapons. Not having something to enchant feels bad. - Add a cooldown reduction cap. - Add a way to reduce spellcast recovery. Add a cap for this recovery. 10-15 second recovery spells are absurd. Let energy be our bottleneck. Or maybe separate spellcast recovery from physical, that way my character isn't just effectively stunned for 10 seconds. - More ways to increase radius for skills or projectile count maybe. I love stuff like that. - Adventures are too short. Some are as short as 2 fight maps, and there isn't a good reason not to take the shorter path, ever. - Adventures need more path options. I don't see a good reason why there are only 2 paths. - Too frequently a rest point on a path is followed by a chest room, or a shrine room making these rest points completely meaningless. I have literally never made use of the rest point regen buff, because it only applies to the subsequent map which is always a peaceful map. - I would like to keep levelling beyond 35, and dungeoning beyond tier 40. After tier 40 is beaten, unlock the 35 cap and the new endless difficulty. Character power is already soft-capped by skillpoint allocation scaling and 150 stat limits. or - Add a character reincarnation feature where they can keep some stats and skillpoints, but make them restart at level 1. This would also make the "Apprentice" enchantment suck less. I would also just increase the maximum effectiveness of this enchantment from 90% to 100% item level requirement reduction. There's no good reason to limit this to 90%.

You don't get to pick your starting party. You have to pay to replace them. You have Human as the only option to start with and 5 classes, so almost no customization. This is not how you start a "party building rpg." There does seem to be a wonderful combat system underneath, but I can't get the bad taste of the start out of my mouth. Give me a build party option to start, with at least 4 races and 7-10 classes (even if they're locked once you start the actual game), and then I'll change this vote. EDIT: I tried to stick with it for awhile... but man, this game is repetitive. There's only a handful of maps, so you're playing the same ones over and over again. Progress is slow, so the grind is pretty crazy. I think I'm done with this.

Edit: Good game except the arena nodes. These are always MUCH MUCH harder and tend to end my runs in defeat. There are some rewards for failure, but they quickly become so pitiful as to be almost nothing. The enemies and dungeons scale pretty harshly as it is, and the arena's just kill it for me. Maybe you're thinking "git gud." Sure, but the formation has to include some squishier units protected in the back row... but in arenas, enemies spawn in all around. It's impossible not to have enemies behind, where they have a big chance to target the glass cannon mage. I even leave the enemy rangers unless there aren't any other enemies to attack, as they rangers are less dangerous than AOE or melee... but it still often ends in defeat. Unless I turn the challenge rating down so low that the rewards for success also are pretty pitiful. Forget this. TL;DR Good game! Try the demo, but keep reading for some things that weren't obvious (at least to me). First, the game is ridiculously dark in some dungeons, as in, can't find the door in the cave dark. Increase the gamma. Brightness maxed and shadows min help, but wow, gamma. And anyone who can learn light magic can eventually learn a torch spell. (Maybe this is not a common issue,) Second, the game organizes things well. For example, skills are grouped by their skill training buildings (temple skills include light and body magic, thieves guild includes perception and disarm traps, etc.) A person in a given class (like ranger) can learn some skills (go to the training buildings for low price), but not others. The little diamonds are showing how many levels of mastery that character can eventually get: basic, expert, master, and grandmaster. Great quality of life and lots of info in one space here. Adventures are divided into map sections and themed rooms. There are several different sections possible. (So far I've seen forest, swamp, cave, and stronghold). But a section like the stronghold appears to always have the exact same stronghold layout. That isn't terrible; I can learn where the treasure chests are and that past that door is the boss. Maybe higher levels have variations... I sometimes run into evil shrine rooms instead of good shrines where I can buy building materials (yes please). I don't think I'll get bored, but it's fair to note. Third, faces and voices. There are lots of custom portraits for creating characters. Free changes to appearance and free skill respec. And it's possible to add your own custom portraits and even voice files (haven't tried either). Voice acting is just short bits from characters getting walloped or single lines from enemies. The portraits and customization are very cool! The voice acting is more in the good attempt category. Fourth, art. I also really appreciate that it isn't stupid retro pixel ugly graphics. Finest you can imagine? Nope, but the first dungeon in the demo doesn't show off the range. Fifth, it's also fair to note that if you stop an adventure partway through, it's going to reset the dungeon. Sometimes real life intrudes, and I didn't want to lose ANY hard won progress. But even dead characters return back in town, and even failing an adventure still gets a % of the rewards. Last, I'm playing on Linux Mint through Proton. It just works! Anyway, the demo will show most everything else. At the modest normal price, I highly recommend buying the game.

Beautiful. The game offers a novel alternative to turn-based combat, where time progresses as actions are performed. The result is wonderful: we have the opportunity to analyze each action in detail, for which the game also provides detailed statistics on each enemy and each of our attacks. The aesthetics are also appealing.

The 'Real-Time with Pause' mechanic works really, really well. Titans is just fun to play. It also treats the player to loads of race, class, and loot options. My only gripe is the one that many here have voiced: Playing the same maps over and over gets pretty repetitive. I made it to 32 hours having an awesome time but that was all I could take without the added discovery of new environments. I'm left wanting more but still appreciative of the experience I did have. Titans of the Past is a sure bet for any blobber fan.

As fan of golden era M&M I want to like game, but simply cannot. To many little things that sips enjoyment out of the game... Lets start with positive: - mechanical party customization – many races, lot of classes (cool) - time moves as you move – I find this probably my favorite Negatives: - game optimization – there is no reason my cpu fan should sound like he needs to take off. - equipment – my cod. Equpment system is so ugly. There is no sorting options (you can filter, but it is like: clear filter, *click* open filtering options, *click* unfilter previous option, *click* filter new option). Icons are small, and I think there is too many slots for equipment. Not many games made me not wanting to check new equipment that I got, and this is one of them. - chaotic rougelite – gameplay system is very rougelike, but it means single adventures don’t have their story anymore… first you go to wall fighting extraplanars, after that you fight in arena in forest fighting rats… next you go to a cave to rest, and after that you are in marketplace fighting greenskins... - limited sets – I don’t know if there is more than 10 dungeons in the game (some with variations) - limited enemy variety – Devs provided ok number of enemy factions but there is lack of variety inside a faction, so you often meet cross-factional parties. Probably the biggest letdown are beasts, as the only bestial enemies that I meet are… the rats (3 types, but still), so they often along the mages etc. - new feature 6 people party mode – It sounded cool… until I found out that increasing party size by even single person simply triples enemy dmg and HP (also I think it increase number of enemy spawns, and rare enemies often get modifiers like “your spells are usless now”). So something that sounded like “I could use that nishe class” for a party, became tool for people for super optimizing. It can provide some WTF moments like: being hit for 160 dmg at level 1, being 1 shoted by lv 1 rat while being level 2, Opening door and seeing special fire rat boss, hiding behind corner and it cast fireball and wiped it’s own entourage (this one was funny thou). - Poor balance – there are many classes, but some just don’t feel as useful as others. It wouldn’t be bad if gameplay didn’t reward rather balanced, and optimized parties (especially for 6 party size). One of my WTF moment was when class offered dual-wielding skill and not weapon that was possible to use in offhand - AI – Ok lets point big elephant in the room. Use of AI for character portraits… I may be more understanding if portraits were better, but some have this deja vu feeling like I seen these somewhere, not identical but very similar, like they feed original and modified it with AI. For sure it would be better if devs made simple face creator in simplistic style of game. - End of support – game reached it’s end of support, so no design flaws will ever be revised, no QoL feature added… I understand a bit, as game wasn’t commercial success, well M&M rpgs fans are probably too small group to support, so If you won’t catch big streamer attention then it is at most passion project. Closing thoughts… I would probably still found many nitpicks, but in the end while I have lot of negative thoughts I still hope that devs will learn from experience and next project will be better. If they make another game that I am interested in I may buy it, but they still need to keep in mind that I am in minority, and many players will probably just blacklist for such sudden EoS. Will I keep playing? Maybe in small doses, but will erase my 6 people squad as playing it is frustrating for me (well golden age M&M games weren’t exactly hard games). EDIT: it seems DEV still provide some bug fixes, so I deleted paragph about it that I missunderstood. tiny "+" for Devs.

The game is pretty fun, but kind of a dead end. The balance is way out of whack and the devs stated (even before they released the final update) that they weren't going to address some of the glaring issues. Which is too bad because there was a lot of potential here, but seeing as they refuse to even fix or change the things that would have brought out that potential, it's no wonder it wasn't a success. And I'm not even talking about the fact it's all assets and AI portraits, I can forgive those, but that there's a very common mission type that basically ends your run unless you completely cheese it or are overleveled (and sometimes even then) is unforgiveable. And even when they did address issues from the demo, they did it in such a boneheaded way that it's a wonder the game was even released. The fact that people wanted to use 6 party members instead of just 4 so the devs allowed it, but if you add a 5th party member enemy damage and health goes up +200% is beyond punishing. Poor babies didn't want players to get what they wanted so they decided that was the way to go. And of course if you go into one of the arenas that is the typical run ender with 6 members then you pretty much just die. It's still very dangerous with just 4 members, but gods help you if you take a full party. Which is pretty wild since everything else with a 4 member party is braindead easy. The fact they didn't bother to do any tuning and just left the game to die on the vine is a pretty sad state of affairs, and a fair indication of whether the game is worth buying or not. Hint: it isn't, not at the current price point. If it was under $10 and some of the garbage decisions they made were at least brought into line with the rest of the game then it'd be fine. Not the worst thing I've ever wasted money on, but it's up there, and it's a real waste.

Two issues. Can't equip two knucle dusters as a monk and the lack of knucle dusters in the game as my character picture I made is of me in a goldish robe with the fuzzies around the neck with a gold cross and two spiked gold knuckle dusters. I feel like a monk should have the option in unarmed to equip two considering monks train their fists and with a pole. And my next and last issues is with the frame drops that happen HEAVY around any map with lots of moving parts. Specifically trees and foliage. If there could be an option to just turn off all movement on static objects like trees and so on that would be game changing and cause my system to probably stop heating up so much and dropping MASSIVE frames on those specific maps. Other than that this game is like perfection in every way. I played the demo. Thought it was good. So I bought it. And I don't regret the purchase. That demo sold it to me instantly. It gives you just enough to let you KNOW that you want it. Okay that's all for this review. Genuine relay on information I've learned from the game and the fixes I know it needs. Runs smoothly overall depending on the level, but because the levels are random and in too set of an order it causes issues on some maps that feature any trees or foliage or moving things. Make the fire static. Make the trees static. The grass and bushes. Have an option for it I mean and I think my game will run pretty smooth. Thank you if you read this and if not. I probably shouldn't expect anything and that's okay. I'll still try and play it how it is, but I know I'd enjoy it more with more frames. Also on AMD it black screens my entire screen if I play at anything above 1080p. And I have a 2k res monitor. Just a little side note I thought I'd add. Okay bye now. Buy the game. Peace.
